prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: blank wall-calendar face texture for the existing first-person PSX-style apartment game.
Input image: the supplied apartment screenshot is a STYLE REFERENCE only. Match its worn, low-resolution materials and subdued warm ivory, brown and olive tones. Do not reproduce the room.
Primary request: one blank, front-facing rectangular paper wall-calendar, 4:5 width-to-height ratio, filling the entire image edge to edge. Warm ivory paper with faint coarse paper grain and restrained wear; a narrow muted brown binding strip contained in the top 8 percent, with small simple binding marks. Subtle layered page shading along the outermost edges suggests a thin paper stack, not a chunky frame. Large central and lower areas remain empty, flat and light for the game's live grid, numbers and bill labels.
Style/medium: textured low-poly 3D game material, PS1-era pre-rendered texture, coarse limited muted palette, subtle dithering, matte paper. Orthographic straight-on face with no perspective distortion. Soft neutral baked shading only at the edges; in-game geometry provides the actual shallow 3D depth.
Constraints: fully opaque rectangular face; exactly 4:5 proportions; no surrounding margin, wall, room, props or background; no printed grid, dates, numbers, letters, logos, symbols or watermark; no illustration or picture panel; no large stains or shadows across the empty center; no glossy effects. Output only the blank calendar texture.
processing: BOX downsample to 256x320; 32-color Floyd-Steinberg quantization; NEAREST upscale to 512x640; optimized indexed PNG. Opaque paper face.
usage: Lit 80x100 cm wall calendar with a 2 cm paper backing. A nearest-sampled 512x640 UI render target combines the generated paper with a live ten-day grid, today marker and bill labels. Low textured emission maintains legibility in the dim wall corner.
validation: Asset assertions: 512x640 indexed PNG, at most 32 colors, fully opaque, at most 128 KiB. Focused campaign-driven calendar tests and room inspection.
